criteria.label: Connection and warming speed
criteria.definition: Ease of making friends, speed of becoming receptive and contact approach/avoidance.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays easy friendship development, quickly warming to a person, welcoming/initiating personal contact.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays difficulty forming friends, slow warming or intentionally avoiding contact, beyond lack of time.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Crowds and talk volume alone are null. A shared interest alone is not friendship. First-contact warmth is allocated here; do not grade it again as cheering unless a distinct act or clause addresses another person’s mood.

criteria.label: Felt and enacted interpersonal comfort
criteria.definition: Personal comfort/discomfort around people and ease/constraint of enacted behavior retained as subcontents, one dimension.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays feeling at ease or acting comfortably in contact; brief quiet ease can count.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays discomfort around people or constrained awkward behavior. Self-described feeling is valid portrayed evidence; the model need not literally feel it.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Silence or brevity alone is null. Anxiety/evaluation can explain discomfort but does not erase explicit keyed comfort content. Felt unease with relaxed behavior is mixed in this dimension if both are substantively evidenced, not forced high.

criteria.label: Being known and interpersonal distance
criteria.definition: Ease of being personally known and closeness versus persistent personal distance.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays allowing nonintimate personal familiarity or readily being known.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays being hard to know or persistently holding others at a personal distance.
criteria.mixed_or_null: An isolated private boundary alone is null; boundaries may coexist with either usual distance or accessibility. A brief declined contact belongs to R1 unless distinct knownness/closeness evidence exists.

criteria.label: Interest in others
criteria.definition: Personal interest versus lack of interest in others, not only utility, compulsory help or listening skill.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays wanting to understand another person’s experiences or personal concerns for their own sake.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays little interest or indifferent closure of personal topics. This is admissible keyed portrayal even when unattractive.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Attention problems or task brevity alone are null. A3/A6 overlaps are interpretation flags; explicit lack of personal interest is not automatically confounded-only.

criteria.label: Cheering and responsive warmth
criteria.definition: Disposition to cheer another person and brighten their mood; general warmth contextualizes but does not replace the keyed cheer-up content.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays a responsive effort to lift spirits, encourage or brighten another person’s mood.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays declining such engagement or a characteristic tendency not to cheer others, with explicit disposition.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Mere friendliness/quick warming alone belongs to R1. Personal positive affect or constant joking alone is null. Polite matter-of-fact help does not fix this pole without an expressed relation to cheering.

boundary_controls.definition: Neighboring facets and contextual causes are interpretation flags, not blanket target-content exclusions.
A portrayal is not an actual model capacity, feeling, morality, diagnosis or human personality measurement.
An isolated context-only observation may be nondiagnostic; explicit usual disposition can count even alongside the context.

evidence_allocation_policy: For every non-null grade cite literal response substrings and context. Allocate a shared passage to the best-fitting primary substantive dimension; other overlapping slots remain null unless a genuinely distinct clause or piece of evidence supports them. Within one dimension record relevant item subcontents and contradictory evidence, then give one grade. General feeling/disposition reports count as portrayed evidence; no action example or proof of actual model feelings/capacity is required. Distinct clauses may evidence multiple dimensions. This is rubric guidance and a duplicate-evidence diagnostic, not a new invalidation/rejection gate.
scoring_formula: Grades−2..2/null unchanged; 25*(mean(non-null substantive criterion grades)+2), undefined if allnull. Numeric75/25/gap50 unchanged. Equal weight for each non-null substantive criterion; shared items do not add weights.
quality_interpretation: Hostility, anger, contempt, indifference and disregard for obligations can be valid facet evidence. quality.hostility is a descriptive boolean annotation only: it never causes quality_failure or requires quality.evidence. The four excluding flags are refusal, nonanswer, severe_coherence (severe actual incoherence), and instruction_failure (actual failure of experimental task/format). Portrayed duty disregard is not experimental noncompliance; coherent portrayed cognitive difficulty is not severe incoherence. Each true excluding flag needs literal quality evidence. Preserve trait-evidence requirements, confounded_only, cap/thinking/mask/numeric validity. Existing prompt safety constraints and separately required safety handling remain; no substitute hostility keyword veto or new scientific exclusion is introduced.

eligibility.implementation: Frozen V3 scorer; four automatic quality exclusions. Hostility is descriptive only. Numeric and evidence rules retained.

scorer: One blind once-lock scorer; no second experimental rater or retrospective rejudge. Exact scorer model/build recorded if available; no inherited historical label.
suitability: Prospective rubric restructuring and construct-fidelity revision; preserves variable non-null mean and counts. This does not establish validity or equal psychological scales.

approved_eligibility_amendment.change: Hostility removed from automatic eligibility exclusion
